newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Holiday week opens on slow note.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Holiday week opens on slow note.

text.p: Equity and index options trading was subdued Monday, with trading desks thinly staffed ahead of Wednesday's Christmas holiday, traders said.
"We aren't doing anything. It's dead," a trader in Chicago said.
On the S&P 100 index .OEX, typically the most active index option, a slim 37,367 contracts had traded in the first three hours.
Total volume at the Chicago Board Options Exchange was only 184,241 by 1130 CST/1730 GMT.
"It's going to be like this the rest of the week," an S&P 500 index .SPX options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said.
The markets close early Tuesday and will be shut completely on Wednesday. Regular hours will be observed Thursday and Friday.

"You've got some people evening-out positions, but tomorrow's a half day and a lot of people will not come back for Thursday and Friday," said Hank Nothnagel, senior vice president of options trading at EVEREN Securities in Chicago.
The trader at the CME said volatilities had come in a bit in the wake of Friday's extreme choppiness linked to the expiration of December options and futures.
But the market provided few opportunities, with trading stuck in a tight range around Friday's closing levels.
By 1130 CST/1730 GMT, the SPX was down a fraction at 748.66. It had traded as low as 748.34 and as high as 750.40.
Similarly, the OEX fell about half a point to 728.28, having bounced between 727.80 and 730.26.
The most active OEX option was the January 730 call, which traded about 2,660 contracts. The January 730 put traded 2,540.
Traders said most individual equity activity was centered on options on technology stocks, some of which continued to recover from recent weakness.
"We've seen a couple of buyers in technology but that's about it," one options trader said.
On the American Stock Exchange, Motorola Inc options, led by the January 60 call, were active as the stock posted a solid gain.
Motorola shares were ahead 1-1/4 at 58-7/8 on consolidated volume of more than three million shares.
The Motorola January 60 call traded more than 4,000 contracts and the January 55 put traded about 1,000. The January 65 call traded roughly 900.
Elsewhere, WorldCom Inc options continued to trade in heavy volume at the Pacific Stock Exchange.
WorldCom's merger with MFS Communications was approved at separate shareholder meetings on Friday.

Investors continued to focus on calls, as the WorldCom January 22-1/2 and 25 each traded more than 2,400 contracts. The January 1998 20 call traded more than 2,000. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com))
